summary: Frontend-only verification of the remote Electron client UI served at GET /api/client-app/index.html. Injected the window.api preload stub + /api/keys/validate mock via add_init_script, passed splash -> key gate -> Configuracoes tab. The 'Atualizacao' (Update/Version) card renders correctly: #app-version = 'v1.0.4' and #app-version-status = 'Você está na versão mais recente.' (populated from the real GET /api/client-version which returns {"version":"1.0.4"}). Also verified served assets contain the card markup (index.html lines 100-101) and renderer.js updateSettingsUI logic (line ~317). No console errors, no page errors, no error elements.

issues: Settings content column is capped at ~740px and left-aligned, leaving ~60% of the viewport empty on wide screens (cosmetic only; the Electron window is narrow so low impact).

critical_code_review_comments: updateSettingsUI() swallows apiGet('/api/client-version') failures with .catch(() => {}), so #app-version-status stays empty if the version endpoint fails. Consider showing a fallback message.
Settings elements are targeted by DOM ids only; no data-testid attributes on the version card (#app-version / #app-version-status were usable, but data-testid would be more robust).
seed_data_creation: None. Used the stubbed window.api config (deviceCode PC-VTEST, version 1.0.4) and mocked POST /api/keys/validate.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To test the remote client UI in a browser you must page.add_init_script the window.api stub + fetch override for /api/keys/validate BEFORE navigating to {BACKEND_URL}/api/client-app/index.html. Splash ~1.6s, key gate prefilled from api.getKey(), click #key-submit, then click .nav-item[data-view="settings"]. Version card verified working in this iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: No defect reproduced. The user-reported missing Update card is present and populated in the currently served UI; the earlier report likely predated the deploy of the updated /api/client-app assets (or the installed Electron build was using a cached/older bundled renderer rather than the remote one).
